headline: SITCON rises to 2: Zyxel GS1900 patch fails against zero-day; WordPress KEV patch due Nov 6; feds warn on cooling-system attacks

bullets.text: New: The Record reports CISA and the FBI are warning critical infrastructure operators to harden cooling and refrigeration systems amid attacks.
New: BleepingComputer reports Truffle Security has launched a program to revoke 1.4 million live secrets.

Still active, Zyxel GS1900, 4 outlets: Help Net Security reports patched switches remained open to an in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441). SecurityWeek says the hacks were a zero-day; The Hacker News says the patch fails to block root command execution.

Due tomorrow, WordPress Core, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports CISA flags a WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a race condition added 2026-11-03, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.

Still active, CVE-2024-27834: The Hacker News reports hackers are exploiting a patched Apple flaw to deliver info-stealing malware, citing CISA. CISA KEV added it 2026-11-04, with a federal due date of 2026-11-18.

Still active, cPGuard, 4 outlets: SecurityWeek reports malicious updates served in an OpsShield supply chain attack. Breaches at DigiCert (identity documents) and Royal Cornwall Hospitals Trust (7,715 staff) were also disclosed today.

actions: Treat Zyxel GS1900 switches as still exposed even after patching: restrict management access, check for compromise, watch for a new fix.
Patch WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 (KEV due 2026-11-06).
Patch Apple devices for CVE-2024-27834 (KEV due 2026-11-18).
Operators of cooling and refrigeration systems: review the CISA/FBI hardening guidance and remove internet exposure of controllers.
Patch Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-104935 (KEV due dates 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13) and check for compromise.
cPGuard users: hunt the backdoor. DigiCert, Chainalysis, mSecure, DreamHost users: follow vendor notices and rotate credentials.
